x: The Eight-Point Formula was announced by Indira Gandhi on 11 April 1969 during the Jai Telangana agitation, while the Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 belongs to the Jai Andhra phase. Option A reverses the two dates; neither formula abolished the Mulki Rules or created the zonal system (that came with the Six-Point Formula of 1973).

The Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 brought Assistant Surgeons and Assistant Engineers under the Mulki rules, adding fuel to the Jai Andhra agitation that had followed the October 1972 Supreme Court judgment upholding the Mulki Rules. The 1969 agitation and the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement came earlier.

Jai Andhra was called off on 1 October 1973, after the Centre proposed the Six-Point Formula on 21 September 1973. 10 December 1972 is when the separate Andhra flag was hoisted, 18 January 1973 is when President's Rule began, and 18 December 1973 is when the Six-Point Formula was approved.
The anti-arrack movement began in Dubagunta (Nellore) in 1991, led by rural women from the Aksharajyothi literacy classes, and is regarded as one of India's most successful women-led movements.

Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal, and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence. Andhra Patrika and Bharati (1924) were Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao's pre-1956 publications, so the other options misattribute them.
